factual_diff_raw.canonical: COTTON CLUB presents WEST ROAD BLUES BAND on September 30, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The venue identifies the group as a pioneering force in Japanese blues, formed in 1972 around members including Takashi Nagai and Junshi Yamagishi, and notes that the band helped drive Japan's 1970s blues boom after opening for B.B. King in Japan and recording from 1975 onward. After suspending activity following Shinji Shiotsugu's death in 2008, the group returned for its 50th-anniversary period in 2025. The venue describes the band as a pioneer of Japan's blues scene, formed in 1972 and part of the 1970s Kansai blues boom. After suspending activity following Shinji Shiotsugu's death in 2008, the band returned at the 2025 Naniwa Blues Festival for its record-debut 50th anniversary. COTTON CLUB states that the September 30 engagement is the band's only performance of 2026 and is made possible by U.S.-based Yamagishi's temporary return to Japan. The standard table-seat music charge is ¥9,000 per person.

factual_diff_raw.canonical: NJPAC presents the world premiere of Sacred Visions: Oru de Oro on Saturday, December 19, 2026 at 7:30 PM in the Victoria Theater. Pianist and composer Michele Rosewoman's New Yor-Uba Ensemble joins choreographer Danys 'La Mora' Perez Prades's Oyu Oro Afro-Cuban Dance Ensemble in a staged realization of Rosewoman's Oru de Oro suite, drawing on Yoruba ceremonial traditions through Afro-Cuban rhythm, contemporary jazz composition, improvisation, movement and storytelling.
factual_diff_raw.candidate: NJPAC presents the world premiere of Sacred Visions: Oru de Oro on Saturday, December 19, 2026 at 7:30 PM in the Victoria Theater. The collaboration brings Michele Rosewoman's New Yor-Uba Ensemble together with Danys 'La Mora' Pérez Prades's Oyu Oro Afro-Cuban Dance Ensemble, joining Rosewoman's jazz-infused suite with choreography rooted in Yoruba and Afro-Cuban traditions. NJPAC describes New Yor-Uba, founded in 1983, as a four-decade bridge between contemporary jazz and Cuban folkloric traditions.
